newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia minister tipped for sack scraps trip - report.
newsitem.headline: Russia minister tipped for sack scraps trip - report.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov has cancelled a planned trip to Georgia this week amid growing speculation that he might lose his job in an expected government reshuffle, Interfax news agency said on Sunday.
The defence ministry in Moscow said it had no information on the reported cancellation. Last week Rodionov called off a visit to Armenia, set for March 3 to 5.
Quoting Georgian defence ministry sources, Interfax said Rodionov had cancelled his trip to Tbilisi "because of uncertainty over whether he would stay in his post or not".

The sources said the cancellation had nothing to do with Rodionov's involvement in an incident in April 1989 when Soviet troops under his command used force to suppress a pro-independence rally in the Georgian capital, earning him the nickname "Butcher of Tbilisi".
About 20 people were killed at that time but Russian officials later exonerated him, saying the true blame lay elsewhere.
Last week President Boris Yeltsin rapped Rodionov, who took over the defence portfolio last July, for publicly "whining" about the problems facing Russia's demoralised, cash-strapped armed forces.
Rodionov, 60, says he supports Yeltsin's plans to reform the military but has called for extra cash to finance them.

Yeltsin said last week he was dissatisfied with the government's failure to tackle Russia's deep-seated economic and social problems and urged Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to shake up his cabinet.
The reshuffle is expected to be announced after Yeltsin gives his annual address to parliament on Thursday.
